solutions.original_learner_prompt:
1. Where was the man, and where is he now? Identify the reference of each pronoun. Explain the number of the subject and predicate noun in the fourth sentence, and identify whose dwelling is mentioned at the close.

   Se mann wæs on ðǣm sǣ. Hē is on ðǣm hofe. Ðā fiscas sindon on ðǣm hofe. Hīe sindon ðæs mannes męte. Ðæt hof is on ðǣre eorðan. Hit is ðæs mannes hof.

models_or_responses: Translation: The creature was in the dwelling. It was an animal. The seed was in the dwelling. It was the creature's food.
Present: Sēo gesceaft is on ðǣm hofe. Hēo is dēor. Ðæt sǣd is on ðǣm hofe. Hit is ðǣre gesceafte męte.
Several creatures, first two sentences only: Ðā gesceafta sindon on ðǣm hofe. Hīe sindon dēor.
Hēo refers grammatically to feminine gesceaft and does not establish the creature's sex.
Hit refers to the seed. Gesceafte is genitive singular in ðǣre gesceafte męte: the creature's food.
solutions.analysis: The transformed predicate dēor is now nominative plural even though its spelling is unchanged. The plural subject selects hīe and sindon. The original final genitive relation resolves gesceafte despite its case syncretism.
solutions.support_boundary: Uses the learner's taught forms, meanings and constructions; no key or author model consulted.

review_coverage.scope: Read every rule and complete noun/article table; retained gender, quantity, syncope, æ/a, w-stem, -nes, -ung/-ing, weak, mann, niht, sǣ and plural-only darkness distinctions. Formal recognition-only plurals and starred sǣ genitive remain bounded.

All ten nominative forms present; no oblique personal form promoted. Every selected present/preterite copula cell remains represented by the compressed complete plural row. Dual subjects use plural verbs; ordinary plurals are not restricted to three or more. Third-singular reference follows grammatical gender and context; third plural is common to genders.

Nominative subjects/predicates, finite agreement, coordinated noun/article phrases, locative on, dependent/nested genitives, accusative objects, dative recipients and fram separation are explained with bounded supplied verbs. Complete target responses are not hidden by removing paradigms.

All44 section:model routes were manually followed to the actual patterns, including lexically retained heofon, exceptional trēo/tācen and separate ǣfen/wæter/nīeten patterns. The cynn/gærs supplied sound notes are supported by the independent preflight and correctly separated from learned historical grammar.

All8 form tasks,6 copula tasks,10 supplied finite frames,46 exact Cook prompts and8 full compositions. The original tasks require role, agreement, person, time, number, stem or relation choices; F08 and source controlled assembly are not falsely counted as unseen production.

Both new connected readings use taught vocabulary/grammar; no old COMP answer sentences are reused. MINI02 demands actual tense/number transformation. MINI01's singular mass predicate męte remains compatible with its plural subject and plural copula.

Read the exact retained first-day source passage, every support row and all8 tasks. Unfamiliar finite forms, passive/subjunctive/resultative/naming constructions and weak heofonan are supplied. READ04/07 are explicitly help checks; other questions distinguish supplied material from new nominal/pronoun/case application. Whole translation remains scaffolded.
